title: What does a minus sign before a bracket do?
description: Two sums with a bracket after a minus sign are worked out, and the second sum is worked out in two ways that give the same value. Keeko doubts that the minus changes every sign inside the bracket.
teaching_notes: One idea: a minus sign before a bracket takes away everything inside it, so every sign inside changes when the bracket is opened. Watch for students who change only the first sign inside the bracket.

video_script.why: A learner sees that a minus sign before a bracket can be handled by working the bracket first or by opening it with every sign changed, and both ways agree.
video_script.substitution: The book's own two sums, the second one worked out in two ways.
video_script.anchor: a minus sign in front of a bracket
video_script.wrong_answer: the minus changes only the first term in the bracket
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko changes only the first sign, so 68 − (18 + 13) becomes 68 − 18 + 13 = 63, but both signs change and the value is 37.
video_script.payoff_line: The values are fifty six and thirty seven

final_answer.spoken: the values are fifty six and thirty seven

never_show: the two values together before the answer beat
maths_rules: A minus before a bracket changes the sign of every number inside.
video_script.design: One idea: a minus sign before a bracket takes away the whole bracket. Assumes working a bracket first. The bracket stays on the stage with its signs coloured. Wrong idea: the minus changes only the first sign.

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A minus sign before a bracket means we take away everything inside the bracket.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Taking away each item inside changes the sign of every number inside it.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>A bracket can also be worked out first, before we take it away.

marks.gv2: the second sum is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, the first sum is forty two plus fifteen minus the bracket eight minus seven.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The second sum is sixty eight minus the bracket eighteen plus thirteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each sum ; the second in two ways
narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find the value of each sum, and the second sum in two ways.
<bookmark mark='s1a'/>In the first sum, the bracket is worked out first.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Eight minus seven is one.
<bookmark mark='s2a'/>Forty two plus fifteen is fifty seven.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Taking away one leaves fifty six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 68 − (18 + 13), way one: bracket first, 18 + 13 = 31, then 68 − 31 = 37

marks.s3a: the bracket 18 + 13 is circled and becomes 31

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>In the second sum, way one works the bracket first, and eighteen plus thirteen is thirty one.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Sixty eight minus thirty one is thirty seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: way two: open the bracket and change both signs: 68 − 18 − 13 = 50 − 13 = 37

marks.s4a: the bracket is opened and the signs of 18 and 13 are both changed

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Way two opens the bracket, and the minus changes the signs inside.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Sixty eight minus eighteen is fifty, and fifty minus thirteen is thirty seven.

marks.ans: the two values are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The values are fifty six and thirty seven.
Both ways give the same value for the second sum.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 68 − 18 + 13 = 63, struck out ; the whole bracket taken away: 68 − 18 − 13 = 37

marks.d3: the bubble is struck out and 68 − 18 − 13 = 37 is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks the minus changes only the first term in the bracket.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>That gives sixty eight minus eighteen plus thirteen, which is sixty three.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>But the whole bracket is taken away, so both signs change and the value is thirty seven.
